protocol.instrument_name: Authority – Supply of specified restricted substances by pharmacists – treatment of acne
protocol.instrument_version: Dated: 05 August 2026 (Dr Kerry Chant, Chief Health Officer; Delegation Number PH380, PH381, PH427). Revokes the instrument entitled 'Authority – Supply of restricted substances by pharmacists relating to the treatment of acne signed 5 August 2025'.
protocol.effective_date: 2026-08-05 (instrument dated 05 August 2026; 'This authority commences on publication.' — publication date not printed; 'This authority is cancelled on 06 August 2027, unless earlier cancelled.')
protocol.legal_basis: Section 10 Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 1966; Clauses 53, 170 and 171 of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008. Issued by Dr Kerry Chant, Chief Health Officer, a duly appointed delegate of the Secretary, NSW Health, pursuant to clauses 53, 170, and 171 of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008 for the purpose of section 10 of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 1966.
protocol.supervision_model: Document's own terminology: an 'approved pharmacist' (holding general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW), employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy', and having successfully completed the specified training requirements) may supply to an applicable patient a restricted substance listed in clause 2 'otherwise than on prescription subject to the conditions in clause 3 of this instrument'.
protocol.scope_summary: NSW Health Authority instrument (legal authorisation, not a clinical practice standard) permitting an approved pharmacist to supply topical Adapalene 0.1-0.3%, Tretinoin 0.025%, Trifarotene 0.005% or Clindamycin 1% otherwise than on prescription for the treatment of acne in an applicable patient (12 years of age or over), subject to the conditions in clause 3. Clinical limits (treatment duration/quantity, age or other factor limitations and circumstances requiring referral) are set by the separate 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne', which is not part of this document.

inclusion.text: The patient is an 'applicable patient' — 'An 'applicable patient' means a patient who is 12 years of age or over.'
'The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 for the treatment of acne.'
The medicine supplied is one of the restricted substances listed in clause 2 — 'This instrument applies to topical forms of: Adapalene 0.1-0.3%; Tretinoin 0.025%; Trifarotene 0.005%; Clindamycin 1%'.

provenance.section_heading: 2) Restricted substances to which this instrument applies:

inclusion.text: Supply quantity does not exceed the duration of treatment specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne, except in the circumstances described in clause 3(c) (smallest available manufacturer's pack).

'The pharmacist acts in accordance with the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne, approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website, including in relation to any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.'
'The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.'

The pharmacist is an 'approved pharmacist' — holds general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW); is employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy'; has successfully completed the specified training requirements; and has provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the expanded-services application form.

Supply occurs at an 'approved pharmacy' — offers the authorised services when an approved pharmacist is present; maintains up-to-date service availability listings via Healthdirect Australia; and has a consultation room that is not used for any other purpose, fully enclosed with adequate privacy, adequate lighting, comfortable ambient temperature, ready access to a hand washing facility and/or medical grade hand sanitisation products, and sufficient floor area for the patient, an accompanying person and the pharmacist.

exclusion.text: The patient is under 12 years of age (not an 'applicable patient': 'An 'applicable patient' means a patient who is 12 years of age or over.').
The medicine is not indicated in clause 2 for the treatment of acne — 'The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 for the treatment of acne.'
The medicine is not a topical form of Adapalene 0.1-0.3%, Tretinoin 0.025%, Trifarotene 0.005% or Clindamycin 1% ('This instrument applies to topical forms of:' the listed substances).

provenance.section_heading: 2) Restricted substances to which this instrument applies:

exclusion.text: The quantity supplied exceeds the duration of treatment specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne and the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack does not exceed the specified quantity (i.e. the clause 3(c) exception does not apply).
The patient and pharmacist are not both physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, or consultation with the patient did not occur prior to supply.
The pharmacist is not an 'approved pharmacist' or the premises are not an 'approved pharmacy' (including failure to meet the consultation room requirements).

An 'age or other factor' limitation on supply set by the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne precludes supply to this patient (clause 3(d) incorporates those limitations into this instrument).

exclusion_exceptions.text: 'If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine exceeds the quantity specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size.'

diagnosis_pathways.name: Supply of a restricted substance for treatment of acne — ordered conditions (clause 3)

steps.description: Clause 3(a): 'The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 for the treatment of acne.' Confirm the presentation is acne and the medicine is a topical form of Adapalene 0.1-0.3%, Tretinoin 0.025%, Trifarotene 0.005% or Clindamycin 1% (clause 2).

gates.criterion: Medicine is a topical form of Adapalene 0.1-0.3%, Tretinoin 0.025%, Trifarotene 0.005% or Clindamycin 1% (clause 2) and is indicated for the treatment of acne

steps.description: Clause 3(b) and 3(c): 'The pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 in a quantity that exceeds the duration of treatment specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne, except in the circumstances described in clause 3(c) of this instrument.' 'If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine exceeds the quantity specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size.'

gates.criterion: Supply quantity does not exceed the duration of treatment specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne (unless the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack exceeds the specified quantity)

steps.description: Clause 3(d): 'The pharmacist acts in accordance with the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne, approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website, including in relation to any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.'

gates.criterion: No age or other factor limitation precludes supply, and no referral circumstance applies under the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne

steps.description: Clause 3(e): 'The pharmacist must provide NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the form at: https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx.' (prerequisite to practising under this instrument, per the 'approved pharmacist' definition).

gates.criterion: Pharmacist has provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the expanded-services application form

steps.description: Clause 3(f): 'The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.' Consultation must occur before any supply is made.

gates.criterion: Patient and pharmacist both physically present at the approved pharmacy premises and consultation occurs prior to supply

steps.description: Definitions (clause 5): 'An 'applicable patient' means a patient who is 12 years of age or over.' Confirm the patient meets the minimum age for supply under this instrument.

gates.criterion: Patient is 12 years of age or over

steps.description: Clause 3(h): 'Pharmacists must make a full clinical record of the consultation using secure digital software. Records must be stored securely for a minimum of seven (7) years or in the case of health information collected while the patient was under the age of 18 years—until the patient has attained the age of 25 years, and must contain:' patient identification details; date of consultation; pharmacist name and Healthcare Provider Identifier - Individual; information relevant to the diagnosis or treatment; any clinical opinion reached; actions and management plan taken; particulars of any medication supplied (name, form, strength and quantity); notes on information or advice given; any consent given; and any referrals made.

Clause 3(j): 'The pharmacist must seek the patient's consent to share a record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one, following consent by the patient. If the patient consents to the disclosure, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation.'

gates.criterion: Patient consents to disclosure of the consultation record to their usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice

treatments.notes: Clause 2: 'This instrument applies to topical forms of: Adapalene 0.1-0.3%'. Supply limited to the treatment of acne (clause 3(a)). Applicable patient must be 12 years of age or over. Quantity/duration is governed by the 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne' (approved by the Chief Health Officer, published on the NSW Health website), a separate document not included in this PDF; clause 3(c) permits supply of the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack if that pack exceeds the specified quantity. Dose, frequency, quantity and duration are NOT printed in this instrument. No pregnancy or lactation caveat is printed in this document; no limitation based on 'age or other factor' beyond the 12-year minimum is printed (clause 3(d) refers those to the Practice Standard).

red_flags.trigger_text: '… circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.' (clause 3(d), as specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne)
'… any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor …' (clause 3(d))
'An 'applicable patient' means a patient who is 12 years of age or over.' — a patient below 12 years of age is not eligible for supply under this instrument.

routine: circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional (clause 3(d) — circumstances as specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne)

review_followup.when: Within a week following the consultation, if the patient consents to the disclosure
review_followup.what: Share the record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one (clause 3(j)).

review_followup.when: For a minimum of seven (7) years following the consultation; for health information collected while the patient was under the age of 18 years — until the patient has attained the age of 25 years
review_followup.what: Store the full clinical record of the consultation securely using secure digital software (clause 3(h), page 2); records must be provided to authorised NSW Health personnel for inspection upon request (clause 3(i), page 3).
'This authority is cancelled on 06 August 2027, unless earlier cancelled.' (clause 7 Cancellation) — the authorisation ceases on this date.

conditions: 'The pharmacist must provide NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the form at: https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx.' (clause 3(e))

'The pharmacist must seek the patient's consent to share a record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one, following consent by the patient. If the patient consents to the disclosure, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation.' (clause 3(j))
'Pharmacists must provide clinical records of consultations upon request to authorised NSW Health personnel for inspection.' (clause 3(i))

open_questions.topic: Dose, frequency, quantity and treatment duration are not printed in this instrument
open_questions.observed: Clause 2 lists topical Adapalene 0.1-0.3%, Tretinoin 0.025%, Trifarotene 0.005% and Clindamycin 1% with no dose, frequency, quantity or duration. Clause 3(b) refers to 'the duration of treatment specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne is a separate document not included in this PDF. Nothing was inferred; treatment dose/frequency/duration fields are left blank.

open_questions.topic: Referral circumstances and age/other factor supply limitations are deferred to a separate document
open_questions.observed: Clause 3(d) incorporates 'any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional' from the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne.
open_questions.why_unclear: The specific trigger wording, thresholds, referral destinations and urgency levels are not printed in this instrument, so red flags RF-1 and RF-2 are qualitative (structured: null) and the referral block lists only routine referral wording. (The companion practice standard NSW_practice-standards-acne.pdf contains a separate referral criteria table; it was not merged into this document's extraction.)

open_questions.topic: Two-column training requirements table garbled in text extraction
open_questions.observed: The 'approved pharmacist' training requirements render as interleaved column fragments, e.g. 'The Queensland / James Cook University's / University of Technology's / Prescribing / Extended community practice / Safe prescribing and OR / training pharmacists course (subject / quality use of / PC6300 only). / medicines course / AND / Clinical / James Cook University's Extended community practice / practice / training and / course (subjects PC6100 and PC6200 only).'
open_questions.why_unclear: Row/column alignment cannot be reconstructed reliably from flat text; INC-7 summarises the requirement as 'the specified training requirements' rather than transcribing the table cells, which appear to offer alternative university course pathways (Queensland University of Technology; James Cook University PC6300, PC6100, PC6200) with AND/OR connectors.

open_questions.observed: '6) Commencement — This authority commences on publication.' The instrument is 'Dated: 05 August 2026' and the instrument it revokes was 'signed 5 August 2025'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The publication date (and therefore the exact effective date) is not stated in the document; effective_date records the date of the instrument plus this note.

open_questions.topic: No notifiable-condition, AIR or adverse-event reporting requirement is printed
open_questions.observed: The instrument requires NSW Health registration details, record retention and consent-based sharing with the patient's usual GP, but is silent on notifiable conditions, Australian Immunisation Register notification and adverse-event reporting.
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required was set to true only for the notifications the document expressly requires (NSW Health details, consent-based record sharing, record production to NSW Health); no other reporting obligation was invented.

open_questions.topic: Pregnancy, lactation and paediatric caveats are not printed
open_questions.observed: The instrument states only the minimum age ('12 years of age or over') and refers other age-based limitations to the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne; no pregnancy or lactation wording appears anywhere in the four pages.
open_questions.why_unclear: No pregnancy/lactation statement exists in this document to transcribe verbatim; none was inferred (e.g. no contraception or teratogenicity wording was added here).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Obtain the current 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Acne' and transcribe its treatment duration/quantity limits, age or other factor supply limitations, and referral circumstances — these govern supply under this Authority but are not printed in this PDF.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clinical limits and referral triggers are incorporated by reference (clause 3(b), 3(d)); the prescribing module cannot evaluate eligibility or escalation without them.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm which approved-pharmacist training pathway local pharmacists have completed (Queensland University of Technology 'Safe prescribing and quality use of medicines course' subject PC6300, and/or James Cook University 'Extended community practice pharmacists course' subjects PC6100 and PC6200, as rendered in the garbled table).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Training requirements are a condition of being an 'approved pharmacist'; the source table is two-column and interleaved in the text extraction, so the exact AND/OR structure must be verified against the PDF.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Verify each pharmacist/pharmacy has completed the NSW Health expanded-services registration (full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx) and displays the consulting pharmacist's name at or near the consultation room.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clause 3(e) and 3(g) are conditions of supply; local go-live must confirm the registration and signage process.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the instrument is current before go-live: dated 05 August 2026, commences on publication, cancelled 06 August 2027 unless earlier cancelled, and revokes the earlier instrument signed 5 August 2025.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Jurisdictionally time-limited authority; commencement (publication) date is not printed, so currency must be checked on the NSW Health website.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local policy for consent-based record sharing with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner within a week, including use of a secure digital messaging platform (footnote 1: 'Use of a secure digital messaging platform is considered best practice'), and the record-retention rule for patients under 18 (retain until the patient has attained the age of 25 years).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Sharing mechanism, local workflow and the under-18 retention clock are left to the pharmacy/practice to operationalise.
